newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher despite intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher despite intervention.

text.p: The won closed firmer versus the dollar on Friday despite a dollar buying intervention by the central Bank of Korea (BOK) in the afternoon, dealers said.
But the BOK denied the intervention, as it routinely does.
The won closed at 823.10 after opening at 824.40. It traded in a range of 819.50 to 824.50.
Export negotiations and expected inflow of dollars when the foreign ownership ceiling in the stock market is raised in October boosted the won, they said.
On October 1, the foreign limit will be eased to 20 percent from the current 18 percent.
"When the dollar reached its low of 819.50, the central bank stepped in limit the dollar's fall," said a local dealer, who declined to be named.
Traders said the won is expected to consolidate on Monday in a range of 822.00 to 826.80 with a base mid-rate of 822.50/60. Today's mid-rate was pegged at 825.80.
